question: Can a bidirectional transformer trained with masked visual token modeling generate images in a few parallel decoding steps with quality beating raster-scan autoregressive transformers?
hypothesis: Treating an image as a raster sequence is neither optimal nor efficient; bidirectional masked modeling with iterative parallel decoding and a concave (cosine) mask schedule will be faster and better.
contributions: MaskGIT: bidirectional transformer for image synthesis trained with Masked Visual Token Modeling
Iterative non-autoregressive decoding in a constant, small number of steps (8 at 256x256)
Mask scheduling function study; cosine works best
Up to 64x faster than autoregressive decoding, SOTA CAS and 512x512 FID
Extension to inpainting, outpainting and class-conditional editing without architecture change

method.summary: Stage 1 reuses the VQGAN tokenizer (16x downsampling, 1024-code codebook). Stage 2 is a 24-layer bidirectional transformer trained to predict randomly masked visual tokens with a sampled mask ratio from a schedule gamma(r). Inference starts from all-[MASK] and over T steps predicts all tokens, samples them, keeps the most confident, and re-masks the rest by gamma(t/T).

models.init_from: inferred: truncated normal initialization (stddev=0.02), from scratch

training.objective: negative log-likelihood (cross-entropy) of masked tokens, Eq 1; mask ratio sampled from schedule gamma(r), cosine default

inference.decoding: iterative parallel decoding: predict, sample, keep most confident, re-mask by gamma(t/T); masking tokens randomly sampled with temperature annealing
inference.prompting: class-conditional (class label); inpainting/outpainting via initial mask constraint

parameters.rejection_sampling: pre-trained ResNet, acceptance rate 0.05 (App B only)
parameters.inpaint_blend: linear blending with input at mask boundary

other.temperature_annealing_details: not given; the paper says its effect is discussed in 4.4 but 4.4 contains no temperature study

limits: Learning rate, schedule, warmup, steps, precision, seeds and FID sample counts are not stated.
Authors concede limited attention size causes semantic/color drift in long outpainting, ignored boundary objects, and oversmoothing or artifacts on faces, text and symmetric objects (App F).
Tokenizer is the unchanged VQGAN; improvements left to future work.
Without guidance MaskGIT's FID at 256 (6.18) is only marginally better than BigGAN-deep (6.95); recall 0.51 is below ADM 0.63 and Improved DDPM 0.62.
The 30-64x speedup is transformer-only wall-clock on an unspecified single GPU.
Text says temperature annealing effect is discussed in 4.4, but no such experiment appears.

terms.definition: Masked Visual Token Modeling: learning to predict visual tokens masked at random with a bidirectional transformer
gamma(r) in (0,1], continuous, decreasing, gamma(0)->1 and gamma(1)->0, giving the fraction of tokens masked
